diagram_math_checks.justification: For fixed b in Delta(S), a in A and o in Omega (Definition lines 48–56), the first box is input (b,a), the second is the probability vector bar b_{b,a} on S, the third is the scalar q(o|b,a) in [0,1], and the positive branch ends at tau(b,a,o) in Delta(S). The zero branch is an unboxed undefined/no posterior annotation, not a probability vector. The abbreviation paragraph explicitly fixes the suppressed parameters.

The T arrow denotes bar b(s prime)=sum_s T(s prime|s,a)b(s) from Definition line 48; the O,o arrow denotes q(o)=sum_{s prime}O(o|s prime)bar b(s prime) from line 50. The arrows are computations, as stated below the figure, not hidden-state transitions or maps between the displayed spaces independent of the fixed parameters. The finite-POMDP definition specifies T as the reward marginal and O as the next-state observation law.

Definition lines 52–56 define tau(o)(s prime)=O(o|s prime)bar b(s prime)/q(o) exactly when q(o)>0, so the upper arrow is correctly directed from q to the normalization result. Nonnegative q excludes a negative branch; q=0 leaves tau undefined, so the lower arrow terminates in text and never a posterior node. Supplier lemma steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 independently prove normalization of bar b and q and the conditional-law interpretation only for q>0.

The accompanying sentence restates Definition line 58: K(C|b,a) is the finite q(o|b,a)-weighted sum of 1_C(tau(b,a,o)) over only positive-likelihood observations. It does not assert distinct posterior points or any transition on a zero-likelihood observation. Supplier lemma step 3.2 proves this is a probability measure independently; no proof or defining clause was altered and the figure is not used as a premise.
